items.title: The races are coming thick and fast 😮‍💨
items.description:
The races are coming thick and fasy 😮‍💨

🇨🇭 Lenzerheide. One of the fastest and most iconic stops on the WHOOP UCI Mountain Bike World Series calendar. ⚡

Huge jumps, technical features, breathtaking alpine scenery and high-speed sections make this a true rider and fan favourite. 👀

When Loris Vergier speaks, you listen 👊

From Vali's dominant home victory to Finn Iles' winning run, revised race schedules, tyre choices and track evolution, we cover it all.

items.title: Is It Selfish to Want to Watch Your Heroes? Ben Cathro Tackles the World Cup's Deadliest Rule
items.description: The 'World Cup Waffle' dives into the controversial qualifying format that keeps the sport's most famous elite racers off the television screen on finals day.( Comments: 128 )

items.title: Exciting But Savage, Should DH Qualifying Change? | World Cup Waffle
items.description:
There is no perfect solution but it's always worth discussing ways to improve the things we love. World Cup DH qualifying has changed a lot in recent years which has made things more exciting but also opened up the possibility  of our favourite racers not making it to finals. This is great in some respects and terrible in others. Series Leader Luca Shaw shocked viewers when he failed to pass through qualifying into finals which has sparked debate about if the rules could be improved? Ben shares his thoughts on the matter.

items.title: I'd Made Peace With Never Winning | Luca Shaw
items.description:
Fresh from securing the first UCI Downhill World Cup victory of his career, Luca Shaw joins us to discuss the long road that led to finally standing on the top step.

After years of being one of the fastest riders in downhill racing, Luca reflects on a career filled with near misses, fastest qualifying times, crashes, mechanicals and missed opportunities when victory seemed within reach. From qualifying fastest as far back as 2018 to finally securing that elusive first World Cup win in Loudenvielle, this conversation explores what it takes to stay motivated when success doesn't come immediately.

We also discuss the pressure of being the last rider on the hill, learning how to recover from mistakes during a race run, the mental side of elite downhill racing and why confidence and experience are just as important as outright speed.

This is a fascinating insight into the reality of competing at the highest level of downhill mountain biking and what happens when years of hard work finally pay off.

items.title: The Team NOBODY Saw Coming | Neko Mullaly on Finding Asa Vermette and Building Frameworks
items.description:
In this episode of Just Ride, Rob Warner and Eliot Jackson sit down with Neko Mulally to talk about building Frameworks Racing from the ground up, from homemade bike prototypes to one of the most talked-about teams in downhill mountain biking.

Neko shares the story behind signing Asa Vermette, bringing Aaron Gwin onto the team, developing World Cup race bikes, and creating a team culture built around trust, performance, and progression. The conversation dives into bike setup, rider development, Hardline, American downhill racing, and what it really takes to compete at the highest level.

They also discuss the future of Frameworks, growing the sport in the U.S., and why simplicity, confidence, and passion still matter in modern downhill MTB.
